docs.intro: How to use Freally Capture, version 1.2.1: build a scene, record it, go live, and everything around them. Every section says which systems a feature works on when it is not all three.
features.audio.body: Every source on its own strip, with noise suppression, a gate, a compressor, EQ and loudness metering — all classic signal processing, with no AI anywhere.
features.audio.title: A broadcast mixer
features.deep.body: Your program as a webcam for video calls, any web page as a source, and exclusive-fullscreen games — Windows first, with every gap stated.
features.deep.title: Virtual camera, browser source, game capture
features.free.body: No paid tier, no account, no telemetry and no model. Your scenes, recordings and stream keys stay on your computer.
features.free.title: Free today, local, no AI
features.guests.body: Invite up to eight guests with a link. They join from a web browser, and their camera and microphone come straight to you, peer to peer.
features.guests.title: Remote guests
features.multistream.body: Go live on Twitch, YouTube, Kick, Facebook, Trovo or any server of your own — several at once — over RTMP, RTMPS, SRT or WHIP, straight from your machine.
features.multistream.title: Multistream, direct
features.record.body: Record with your graphics card's hardware encoder or losslessly in Capture's own format, on up to six audio tracks, with splitting, chapter markers and crash-safe files.
features.record.title: Multi-track recording
features.safety.body: Stage changes in the preview before they go live, check everything with a pre-flight, and keep alarms, encoder failover and a panic button ready.
features.safety.title: Studio Mode and safety
features.scenes.body: Build scenes from displays, windows, games, cameras, web pages, media, images and text, and compose them live on the graphics card with filters and transitions.
features.scenes.title: Scenes on the GPU
features.title: What is in it
featuresPage.cards.audio.body: Noise suppression, gate, compressor, limiter, parametric EQ and de-esser on every strip, with ducking, an auto-mixer, loudness normalization, a soundboard and podcast recording. Classic signal processing, with no AI.
featuresPage.cards.audio.title: A broadcast audio console
featuresPage.cards.automation.body: Rules, macros and variables; MIDI and OSC controllers; a touch panel and tally lights on your phone; PTZ cameras; a show rundown; a WebSocket API for Stream Deck; Lua scripts and plugins. All off by default.
featuresPage.cards.automation.title: Automation and control
featuresPage.cards.deep.body: Your program as a webcam for video-call apps; any web page rendered as a source; and exclusive-fullscreen games through a hook you approve game by game. Windows first, with the gaps stated below.
featuresPage.cards.deep.title: Virtual camera, browser source, game capture
featuresPage.cards.effects.body: Chroma key, color correction, LUTs, masks, a family of blurs, 3D tilt and your own WGSL shaders, on each source. Cut, fade, slide, stinger, luma wipe and a move transition that glides items from scene to scene.
featuresPage.cards.effects.title: Filters and transitions
featuresPage.cards.guests.body: Up to eight guests join from a link, in a web browser, with nothing to install. A green room, private cues, each guest's connection at a glance, and an automatic grid with nameplates.
featuresPage.cards.guests.title: Remote guests from a browser
featuresPage.cards.multistream.body: Go live on several platforms at once over RTMP, RTMPS, SRT or WHIP, with no relay service in between. Each target reconnects on its own, so one failing never takes down the rest.
featuresPage.cards.multistream.title: Multistream, straight from your machine
featuresPage.cards.private.body: No account, no telemetry and no cloud service of ours. Your recordings and stream keys stay on your computer, and no filter uses a model: every one is classic signal processing.
featuresPage.cards.private.title: Local, private, no AI
featuresPage.cards.recording.body: Hardware encoders, with x264 as a fallback, to MP4, MKV, MOV or WebM, or Capture's own lossless format; up to six audio tracks; a clean file for each source; recordings that survive a crash, and a repair on the next launch.
featuresPage.cards.recording.title: Recording that survives
featuresPage.cards.replay.body: A rolling replay buffer that saves the last moments with one key, and a replay source that rolls them back into the show at full, half or quarter speed. A clip trimmer exports without re-encoding when it can.
featuresPage.cards.replay.title: Instant replay
featuresPage.cards.safety.body: A pre-flight before going live, alarms for silence, clipping, a frozen picture and a filling disk, encoder failover mid-show, a panic button, a rehearsal mode that sends nothing, and a quit that finishes everything in order.
featuresPage.cards.safety.title: Broadcast safety
featuresPage.cards.scenes.body: Displays, windows, games, webcams and capture cards, web pages, media, playlists, images, text, timers and test signals, composed live on the graphics card. Nested scenes, groups, shared sources, a vertical 9:16 canvas, and undo for every edit.
featuresPage.cards.scenes.title: Scenes and sources on the GPU
featuresPage.cards.studio.body: Stage the next shot in the preview and send it to the program when it is ready. A multiview, fullscreen projectors on any display, downstream keyers over every scene, and a stats dock with real numbers.
featuresPage.cards.studio.title: Studio Mode and monitoring
featuresPage.cards.title: What version 1.2.1 does
featuresPage.compare.asOf: Capture's price is today's: it is free today, and future versions may be sold. The other products change too; this table is as of 2 October 2026.
featuresPage.compare.intro: Freally Capture next to the commercial studios people use to stream and record. Capture's column is the released version, 1.2.1. Every cell for another product comes from its maker's own pages, checked on 2 October 2026, and prices are US list prices as of October 2026.
featuresPage.compare.note.channels: as channels, AVI or WAV only
featuresPage.compare.obs: OBS Studio is free and open source too, runs on all three systems, and has SRT, WHIP, a virtual camera, a replay buffer and six audio tracks. Streaming to several platforms at once needs a third-party plugin there; in Capture it is built in, along with guests who join from a browser.
featuresPage.compare.price.xsplit: $14.99 a month, $59.99 a year or $119.99 once
featuresPage.compare.row.direct: …straight from your computer, with no relay service in between
featuresPage.compare.row.guests: Guests join from a web browser
featuresPage.compare.row.multistream: Streams to several platforms at once
featuresPage.compare.row.systems: Runs on Windows, macOS and Linux
featuresPage.compare.row.tracks: Several audio tracks in one recording
featuresPage.compare.row.vcam: A virtual camera for video calls
featuresPage.compare.summary: What Freally Capture has that they don't: it is the only desktop app here that runs on Linux as well as Windows and macOS, and the only one that is free. Four of the six need an account and four have AI features; Capture has neither, and it multistreams straight from your computer, where Streamlabs and Restream relay your stream through their own servers.
featuresPage.compare.theyWin: Where they win: Wirecast Pro records up to 8 audio tracks to Capture's 6, and Streamlabs Ultra takes up to 11 guests or cameras and Ecamm up to 10, to Capture's 8. Streamlabs, XSplit, vMix, Wirecast and Ecamm all have a virtual camera; Capture's works on Windows only in 1.2.1 and is not yet code-signed.
featuresPage.compare.title: Side by side with the commercial studios
featuresPage.free.body: Everything Freally Capture does today is free, for everyone: no paid tier, no subscription, no account, no watermark and no trial that runs out. What you record and stream is yours.
featuresPage.free.title: Free today
featuresPage.lead: A live-streaming and recording studio on your own computer: scenes composed on the graphics card, multi-track recording, and multistream to every platform at once, straight from your machine.
featuresPage.limits.ai: It has no AI features — no AI background removal, captions or highlight clips — by design.
featuresPage.limits.browser: The browser source shows a page's picture but not its sound yet.
featuresPage.limits.cursor: Cursor effects and the keyboard and mouse input overlay work on Windows only.
featuresPage.limits.downloads: There are no downloads on this site, and none on this page.
featuresPage.limits.game: Game capture works on Windows only and copies Direct3D 11 games; HDR and Direct3D 12 games fall back to window capture.
featuresPage.limits.heading: The limits, stated plainly
featuresPage.limits.intro: A feature list that hides its gaps is not worth reading. Everything above is in version 1.2.1, and this is what it does not do.
featuresPage.limits.signed: The virtual camera's system component and the browser runtime are not code-signed yet, and two live tests are still owed: the camera inside a real video call, and game capture in a protected game.
featuresPage.limits.title: What 1.2.1 does not do
featuresPage.limits.vcam: The virtual camera works on Windows only; the macOS and Linux cameras are not in this release.
featuresPage.numbers.encoders: families of hardware encoder: NVENC, Quick Sync, AMF, VAAPI and VideoToolbox
featuresPage.numbers.intro: Each figure is what version 1.2.1 does, counted from its code and its changelog. Nothing is rounded up.
featuresPage.numbers.platforms: platforms built in — Twitch, YouTube, Kick, Facebook and Trovo — plus any server of your own
featuresPage.numbers.protocols: streaming protocols: RTMP, RTMPS, SRT and WHIP
featuresPage.numbers.systems: operating systems: Windows, macOS and Linux
featuresPage.version: This page describes Freally Capture 1.2.1, the released version: everything on it is in 1.2.1, and nothing planned for later is on it.
featuresPage.why.dsp.body: Noise suppression, keying and tone-mapping are formulas, not models. The same input and the same settings give the same result, and nothing is downloaded to make them work.
featuresPage.why.dsp.title: Classic signal processing
featuresPage.why.honest.body: When a feature works only on one system, is not code-signed yet, or still owes a live test, the app, the changelog and this page say so.
featuresPage.why.honest.title: Honest about its gaps
featuresPage.why.local.body: A streaming tool should never become "connect your channel". There is no account to make and no relay of ours in the middle: your stream goes from your computer to the platforms you chose.
featuresPage.why.local.title: It stays on your machine
featuresPage.why.owned.body: The compositor, the audio engine and the lossless recording format are Capture's own. The codecs the platforms require come from ffmpeg, downloaded the first time you need it rather than bundled.
featuresPage.why.owned.title: Its own engine
featuresPage.why.safe.body: Every network listener, every automation and every risky capture is off by default. Game capture asks you for each game, and a shared scene collection can never carry that permission.
featuresPage.why.safe.title: Off until you turn it on
featuresPage.why.title: Why it is built the way it is

hero.headline: Record and stream like a studio. One clean app.
hero.sub: A live-streaming and recording studio for Windows, macOS and Linux. No accounts, no telemetry and no cloud service of ours: your stream goes straight to the platforms you choose.
honest.downloads.body: This site describes Freally Capture; it does not distribute it. There is no download page, link or button, and the source code is private.
honest.downloads.title: There are no downloads here
honest.network.body: Your streams go to the platforms you set up. A remote-guest session's handshake crosses a public signalling service; a chat overlay reads a channel's public chat; ffmpeg and the browser runtime are downloaded the first time you need them; the app checks for updates; and a problem report goes only when you press Send on its page. Apart from the update check, each happens only because you set it up.
honest.network.title: What does go online
honest.signed.body: The virtual camera's system component and the browser source's runtime are not code-signed yet, and two live tests are still to be done: the camera inside a real video call, and game capture in a protected game. The changelog says so in the release that added them.
honest.signed.title: Two components are not code-signed yet
honest.title: The things most sites put at the bottom
honest.windows.body: In 1.2.1 the virtual camera, game capture and cursor effects work on Windows only, and the browser source has been verified on Windows first. The rest of the studio runs on Windows, macOS and Linux.
honest.windows.title: Some of the newest features are Windows-only
ladder.intro: Every version of Freally Capture so far, from the foundation to the current release. The changelog has the details of each one.
ladder.note: Every version listed is done. What comes after 1.2.1 is planned privately and appears here when it ships. None of them is a download on this site.
ladder.rung.v0.10.0: The foundation: the desktop app's shell over its own engine, the build checks on Windows, macOS and Linux, and this site.
ladder.rung.v0.200.0: Automation and capture depth: rules, macros, MIDI and OSC control, a LAN touch panel, tally lights, PTZ cameras and a show rundown, plus punch-in zoom and HDR-to-SDR tone-mapping.
ladder.rung.v0.25.0: Capture: screens, windows and webcams on Windows, macOS and Linux, live in the preview.
ladder.rung.v0.300.0: New sources and overlays: instant replay, a gapless playlist, a title and scoreboard designer, an audio visualizer, a stats overlay, a split timer, an input overlay, LAN ingest and Freally Link.
ladder.rung.v0.40.0: The GPU compositor: scenes built from sources and composed on the graphics card, with filters such as chroma key, color correction, LUTs and blur.
ladder.rung.v0.400.0: Compositor depth: 3D corner-pin, downstream keyers, freeze-frame, more blurs, the move transition, a WGSL shader studio, bezier masks and track-matte stingers.
ladder.rung.v0.500.0: Audio production: output routing, a ducking matrix, an auto-mixer, loudness normalization, a parametric EQ, a soundboard, podcast recording and CLAP and VST3 plugin discovery.
ladder.rung.v0.55.0: Audio and recording: a mixer with up to six tracks and classic-DSP filters, and multi-track recording with hardware encoders and Capture's own lossless format.
ladder.rung.v0.56.0: A native GPU preview: the program painted straight from the compositor, with no lag.
ladder.rung.v0.600.0: Recording and replay depth: per-source ISO recording, a clip trimmer, recording with transparency, automatic markers, a post-record pipeline, an integrity check and SMPTE timecode.
ladder.rung.v0.70.0: The studio: streaming to Twitch, YouTube, Kick, Facebook and Trovo with automatic reconnects, Studio Mode with transitions, hotkeys, profiles and a stats dock.
ladder.rung.v0.700.0: Streaming insight: a network simulator, a rehearsal mode, a dropped-frame timeline, a session report, an encoder benchmark, and sources shown only on the stream or only in the recording.
ladder.rung.v0.800.0: Remote guests and show production: up to eight guests, a green room, cues, a connection-quality dashboard, a telestrator, a teleprompter and automatic guest grids.
ladder.rung.v0.85.0: Streaming depth: multistream to several platforms at once, SRT and WHIP, a vertical canvas, nested scenes, a replay buffer and a chat overlay that needs no sign-in.
ladder.rung.v0.90.0: Remote control and extensions: a password-protected WebSocket API, browser docks, sandboxed Lua scripting and a plugin SDK, all local and off by default.
ladder.rung.v0.900.0: Studio management: scene packs, compare and merge, named snapshots, portable mode, one-file backups, a theme editor and dock layouts.
ladder.rung.v0.910.0: The teleprompter, reworked: pause chips, a start countdown, BPM pacing, read-aloud, and autocomplete in all 18 languages.
ladder.rung.v0.95.0: Distribution: a signed auto-updater, audio captured per application, and the licence agreement on first run.
ladder.rung.v0.96.0: A studio for everyone: 18 languages, full keyboard and screen-reader support, a first-run setup wizard, a command palette and themes.
ladder.rung.v0.97.0: Scene authoring and monitoring: undo and redo, an OBS scene-collection importer, alignment guides, a keying workbench, a multiview and projectors.
ladder.rung.v0.98.0: Broadcast safety: a go-live pre-flight, alarms, a source-health dashboard, encoder failover, crash-safe recording, a panic button and a quit guard.
ladder.rung.v0.99.0: Sources, devices and calibration: test signals, A/V sync calibration, timers and clocks, text from a file, a hotkey map, deinterlacing and camera controls.
ladder.rung.v1.0.0: The first stable release: every planned feature, plus a Starting Soon countdown, background music, a social bar and a featured chat banner.
ladder.rung.v1.1.0: A shareable MP4, written beside each lossless recording when it stops.
ladder.rung.v1.2.0: Deep capture and the web: a virtual camera, a true browser source and game capture, Windows first.
ladder.rung.v1.2.1: The audit: no new features, a full security and correctness pass, and the three 1.2.0 additions made to work.
ladder.title: Version by version
site.tagline: Record and stream like a studio — scenes, sources, multistream, one clean app.
what.p1: Going live usually takes one app to capture, another to mix the sound, a service to send the stream to several platforms, and an account with each of them.
what.p2: Freally Capture is one studio on your own computer. Build a scene from your screen, windows, cameras, media and overlays; compose it on the graphics card; record it on up to six audio tracks; and stream it to several platforms at once, straight from your machine with no relay in between.
what.p3: It needs no account and sends no telemetry. What leaves your computer is the stream you chose to send, plus the few connections you switch on yourself — each listed plainly in the documentation.
